The ASU power requirement assumed for this report is 420 kWh/ton-O (including the MAC, booster compressor, and auxiliaries, on a 100 percent 2 pure O basis). 2 3.1.2.1 Residual Nitrogen Injection The residual N that is available after gasifier O and N requirements have been met is 2 2 2 compressed and sent to the CT. Since all product streams are being compressed, the ASU air feed pressure is optimized to reduce the total power consumption and to provide a good match with available compressor frame sizes. 64 COST AND PERFORMANCE BASELINE FOR FOSSIL ENERGY PLANTS VOLUME 1: BITUMINOUS COAL AND NATURAL GAS TO ELECTRICITY Increasing the diluent flow to the CT by injecting residual N from the ASU can have several 2 benefits, depending on the design of the CT:  Increased diluent increases mass flow through the turbine, thus increasing the power output of the CT while maintaining optimum firing temperatures for syngas operation. This is particularly beneficial for locations where the ambient temperature and/or elevation are high and the CT would normally operate at reduced output.  By mixing with the syngas or by being injected directly into the combustor, the diluent N 2 lowers the firing temperature (relative to natural gas) and reduces the formation of thermal NOx. In this report, power augmentation was accomplished by diluting the fuel gas with excess N 2 from the ASU and in some cases, also with steam, until a combustion turbine output of 232 MWe was attained. 3.1.2.2 Air Integration Air integration can provide a modest overall plant efficiency benefit. However, there are ASU operability complications introduced by air integration, particularly at startup. Based on discussions with several ASU vendors, it was decided that the operability issues outweigh the potential efficiency benefits; for this study, air integration is not used for any cases. 3.1.2.3 Elevated Pressure ASU Experience in Gasification The Buggenum, Netherlands, unit built for Demkolec was the first elevated-pressure, fully integrated ASU to be constructed. It was designed to produce up to 1,796 tonnes/day (1,980 tpd) of 95 percent purity O for a Shell coal-based gasification unit that fuels a Siemens 2 V94.2 CT. In normal operation at the Buggenum plant, the ASU receives all its air supply from and sends all residual N to the CT.
